title: Hassler Roma vs Bulgari Rome: Tradition or Modern Energy? (2026) | Suites With Keith
description: Hotel Hassler Roma vs Bulgari Hotel Roma, compared by a travel advisor who visited both in October 2026: traditional or modern, room sizes, rooftop dining, gym and spa, and who each one suits.

hero.alt: The Spanish Steps and Trinità dei Monti at sunrise, with Hotel Hassler Roma at the top of the Steps
A Bulgari Hotel Roma terrace table under a white umbrella at sunset, looking over trees and rooftops

sub: Rome’s grand-hotel tradition at the top of the Spanish Steps, or a modern, lively hotel of marble and mosaics by the Mausoleum of Augustus. Here is how I would choose.

choose.h3: If you love classic, traditional luxury
choose.lead: A very nice, very traditional grand hotel right at the top of the Spanish Steps, with a Michelin-starred restaurant on the roof and a beautiful one in the courtyard.
choose.alt: A Hotel Hassler Roma bedroom with a fabric-covered canopy bed, damask walls and a gilded frame

choose.h3: If you want space, energy and a gym
choose.lead: Spectacular. Base rooms the size of junior suites elsewhere, incredible mosaics, a lively, sophisticated scene and the biggest gym I saw in Rome.
choose.alt: A round stone mosaic above the bathtub in a Bulgari Hotel Roma bathroom

band.h2: Do you want Rome’s grand-hotel style, or marble, mosaics and a buzz?
paras: The Hassler is a very traditional hotel, and that’s the appeal. You are right at the top of the Spanish Steps, and you eat on the roof at a Michelin-starred restaurant with the rooftops of Rome below you.
The Bulgari is the opposite mood: very modern, lots of marble, and lively. The base rooms are very large, and there are more places to eat and drink than I could count.
If you love classic luxury and want the Steps outside your door, pick the Hassler. If you want room to spread out, a gym and a spa now, and a hotel with energy, pick the Bulgari.

guide.alt: The Bulgari Hotel Roma rooftop at sunset, a brick walkway under green arches lined with lounge seating
paras: The dining is a highlight at the Hassler: a Michelin-starred restaurant on the roof, and a beautiful restaurant in the courtyard that is a calmer place to eat than the streets outside.

The Bulgari has a beautiful rooftop bar and pizza restaurant, another bar on the floor below it, and more. Downstairs there’s a classic Roman trattoria with dishes that are actually affordable, like €18 pastas.

guide.alt: A Bulgari Hotel Roma bedroom with a tall upholstered headboard and a Bvlgari throw on the bed
paras: The Bulgari’s base rooms are what other hotels would sell as a deluxe room or a junior suite, so the entry rate already buys real space. I’ll tell you when a higher category is worth it.
The Hassler’s rooms are very traditional: canopy beds, damask walls, crystal lamps. Some bathrooms have windows over the rooftops to St. Peter’s.

guide.alt: The Bulgari Hotel Roma gym, with racks, benches and plates against warm wood paneling
paras: This is the clearest difference today. The Hassler is building a large new wellness and gym area that opens in 2027. Until then, if a spa and gym matter, I point people to the Bulgari or the Corinthia.
The Bulgari has the biggest gym I saw in Rome, massive and with serious equipment, plus a spa.

guide.alt: A freestanding tub in a black marble Hotel Hassler Roma bathroom, with windows over the rooftops to St. Peter’s
paras: The Hassler is right above the Spanish Steps. You can’t get much more iconic, or more central, but the Steps draw crowds from morning to night.
The Bulgari is right next to the Mausoleum of Augustus, which is almost done with its renovation. It is busy outside too. For quiet, the Eden is the one I would pick.

faq.q: Which is better, the Hassler or the Bulgari?
faq.a: It depends on your style. The Hassler for very traditional luxury at the top of the Spanish Steps and Michelin-starred dining on the roof. The Bulgari for very large base rooms, modern design, a lively scene and the biggest gym in Rome.

faq.q: Which has a spa and gym?
faq.a: The Bulgari, with the biggest gym I saw in Rome plus a spa. The Hassler’s new wellness and gym area opens in 2027.
The Bulgari. Its base rooms are what other hotels would call deluxe rooms or even junior suites. The Hassler’s rooms are classic and very traditional.
For a Michelin star, the Hassler’s Michelin-starred restaurant on the roof. For variety, the Bulgari: a rooftop bar and pizza restaurant, more bars, and a trattoria with €18 pastas.
No. At both you step out into busy streets, and the Hassler is right at the crowded Steps. For quiet in the middle of Rome, I pick the Eden or the Corinthia.
